explanation: Mendel's monohybrid crosses showed that recessive traits disappear in the F1 generation only to reappear in the F2 generation, proving that traits are inherited as discrete particles rather than blended.

questions.q: Which generation in Mendel's monohybrid cross first shows the reappearance of the recessive phenotype?
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the recessive phenotype is hidden in the F1 generation and reappears in the F2 generation after F1 self-pollination.
